items.heading: Bds Is a 5
items.text: BDS is a 5-year programme, 4 years of academic and clinical coursework followed by a mandatory 1-year rotating internship, regulated by the dental council structure, now transitioning to the National.

visuals.title: Evidence summary for Bds Is a 5

visuals.alt: Checklist visual explaining 329: 329-333 BDS colleges are currently recognised in India.
visuals.caption: Evidence from 329.

items.text: 329-333 BDS colleges are currently recognised in India, offering roughly 27,600-27,700 seats a year, a network built up rapidly through private and deemed-university expansion, not through matching clinical demand.

items.heading: Only Around 52
items.text: Only around 52-60 of those colleges are government-run (about 3,958 seats). The remaining roughly 23,600+ seats sit in private and deemed colleges, most of them charging fees that are 15 to 100+ times higher than a government seat.

items.heading: The Regulator Itself Has Changed
items.text: The regulator itself has changed shape over this, the Dental Council of India, which oversaw this expansion, was replaced by the National Dental Commission from 19 March 2026, a signal that the old licensing and college-approval structure needed an overhaul.
